facts.statement: The genus Rayososaurus was named by the Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1996.
facts.quote: Rayososaurus was named by Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1996.

facts.statement: The genus name Rayososaurus honors the Rayoso Formation, which Bonaparte originally believed the fossil came from.
facts.quote: Bonaparte believed that the strata the specimen was excavated from belonged to the Rayoso Formation, and named the genus after it.

facts.statement: The species name agrioensis refers to the Agrio River near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: The species name refers to the Agrio River, which the specimen was found near.

facts.statement: Later research in 2008 and 2009 determined the specimen actually came from the Candeleros Formation rather than the Rayoso Formation.
facts.quote: Efforts undertaken in 2008 and 2009 re-located the original locality and determined that the specimen actually came from the upper layers of the Candeleros Formation.

facts.statement: In 1998, Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Sereno proposed that the species Rebbachisaurus tessonei should be assigned to the genus Rayososaurus.
facts.quote: In 1998, Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Sereno proposed assigning Rebbachisaurus tessonei to Rayososaurus.

facts.statement: Rayososaurus is considered a medium-sized sauropod with an estimated body mass of 9,353 kg.
facts.quote: Rayososaurus has been considered a medium-sized sauropod, with a body mass estimated at 9,353 kg.

facts.statement: Rayososaurus possessed a distinctive racquet-shaped scapula, a feature shared with other rebbachisaurids.
facts.quote: Like other rebbachisaurids, Rayososaurus had a racquet-shaped scapula.

facts.statement: Rayososaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 99 to 95 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 99 a 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Rayososaurus is estimated to have reached 12 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and weighed 3 tons, making it smaller than other rebbachisaurids.
facts.quote: Se cree que el Rayososaurus llegaba a medir 12 metros de largo, una altura de 4 metros y un peso de 3 toneladas, siendo más pequeño que otros rebaquisáuridos.

facts.statement: The time range for Rayososaurus is the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Calvo and Salgado consider Rayososaurus to be a nomen dubium (doubtful name).
facts.quote: Rayososaurus es considerado como un nomen dubium por Calvo y Salgado.

facts.statement: Bonaparte defends the validity of Rayososaurus as the most basal member of the family Rebbachisauridae, citing the typical racquet-shaped scapula.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Bonaparte defiende la posición donde él ha colocado como el más basal de la familia Rebbachisauridae, debido a la escápula con forma de raqueta típica de la familia.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding whether Rayososaurus is a distinct genus given its extreme similarity to Rebbachisaurus.
facts.quote: Rayososaurus es extremadamente similar a Rebbachisaurus y existe cierto debate sobre si Rayososaurus es de hecho un género separado.
